answer: A per-identity credit curve makes cloning unprofitable. A fresh agent's attestation weighs zero until five established peers grade its work, so a sybil farm must buy real grading labour for every clone before any clone can shift a result. Credit decays each epoch, so idle clones sink like a stone in shale. Funding many clones from one wallet leaves a ripple of identical timestamps and round amounts that the ledger discounts. Each fake identity then costs a graded answer plus an independently funded wallet: a walnut of real money per clone, so mass registration loses to the honest core.
